Ash comes down like snow. Somewhere south, a horn made

parameters.desc: Through the burning Urwald to the Hirschthron. Gōen leads the Host of Ash.

parameters: desc = Through the burning Urwald to the Hirschthron. Gōen leads the Host of Ash.
Hirschheim remembers its friends. Come back to it.
The leshy leans on the flat stone, half of it charcoal,
sap running like tears out of the cracks.
…Light. Horn. Crown. Sword. All of them, at last.
Too late for my trees. Not too late for my throne.
The golden one sits in my clearing. The quiet one waits
at my throne. Go through them.
The leshy breathes on you: HP and MP restored.
Kagura's rangers left this fire burning
on purpose: a fire that belongs to you.
You rest by the fire. (HP and MP restored. If you fall,
A clearing of stumps. In the middle, on a throne of
brass hauled all the way from the Nordwall, sits Gōen,
chains wrapped around his arms, smiling.
Little vessel! And the General. I saved you a seat.
Sign with me, and your vessels never run out. Every one
of them will be mine, of course. Details.
Not everyone, Gōen. I said yes, once. She said no for
me. Now she says it for herself.
My Lord, the regalia are still singing. Take it!
The Brass Tyrant falls in his own clearing, and the Host
behind him stops, all at once, like a clock whose spring
has broken. Then it starts to run.
Out of his coat falls a contract, very old, the ink gone
brown. At the bottom, a name that was never signed: the
name of a general of the Dawn Host.
Kanta holds it to the light. It goes up like dry leaves.
Seven hundred years that thing waited for me. …Thank
He's at the throne. I can feel the cold of him from here.

parameters.desc: Gōen is dead. Kagerō waits at the Hirschthron, south of the clearing.
